sermon.title: Can a Baptized Believer be “Not Right” with God? 03/04/2018
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer uses Simon the sorcerer in Acts 8 to show that a person can believe and be baptized yet not be right with God. Simon never repented of wanting to be looked up to. He lays out believing, repenting and baptism, the Spirit as a separate experience, and the lake-of-fire sins, but stresses hope: repentance keeps working and God finishes what he began.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: A garbled minister’s name is marked [unclear] (“Mr. Pentecost”). Kept as spoken: Samaria’s history as told (Assyria and Babylon mixed together) (1:20). Point to check: over fifty homosexuals led to Christ. Sensitive content kept as spoken: Native American sweat-lodge drug witchcraft; anger at child sexual abuse, “I just want to beat”; porn stars “high paid prostitutes”; a list of sexual sins that send people to the lake of fire; a homosexual man getting a 16-year-old drunk and having sex with him, removed from church (27:30–29:30).
